newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt sees FY97 at low end of goals.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt sees FY97 at low end of goals.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc said it expects fiscal 1997 results to be at the low end of its targeted annual earnings growth rate of 12 to 15 percent.

"We remain committed to our long-term goals of 12 to 15 percent compounded earnings growth, but overall fiscal 1997 operating results will likely be at the lower end of that range," said Ray Holman, Mallinckrodt chief executive.

The chemicals and healthcare company Tuesday reported fiscal second-quarter profits from continuing operations were $44.1 million, up from $38.3 million in the same period a year ago. Quarterly sales rose eight percent to $571.1 million.

The anticipated results do not include potential impact from previously announced strategic initiatives related to the animal health business and the Tastemaker flavors joint venture, the company said.

Last August, Mallinckrodt said that, in cooperation with its joint venture partner, Hercules Inc, the company would seek a buyer for the Tastemaker flavors business. It also said it would begin exploring strategic options for its animal health division, Mallinckrodt Veterinary, with divestiture preferred. "Both initiatives are progressing according to expectations," Mallinckrodt said.

For the second quarter, the company said its human healthcare segment reported a sales increase of 12 percent to $372.4 million. Operating earnings were $68.4 million, equal to the prior year second quarter. "Top line growth in the company's healthcare segment remains quite strong, but price erosion in the hospital products area negatively affected margins," it said.

In specialty chemicals, quarterly sales were flat at $80.6 million, while operating earnings were $6.0 million, up nine percent. "Improved plant performance and cost containment initiatives contributed to increased earnings," it said.

In the animal health segment, second quarter sales were $118.1 million, up two percent from the same period a year ago. The animal health segment had operating earnings of $9.6 million, compared with $4.2 million during the same period a year ago. "Prior year results included a $3.7 million charge for purchased research and development relating to the acquisition of Syntro Corp," the company said.
Overall second-quarter earnings included $5.8 million in pre-tax earnings from the Tastemaker joint venture, compared with $5.9 million in the prior year second quarter, it said.
